fields.verdict: cross-sectional; before/after or trend (evaluation or monitoring defensible)
fields.why: A routine NIS-Child coverage report; the only target claim is one Discussion sentence (unvaccinated 0.9% meets the HP2030 <1.3% objective), with other HP2030 targets only in table notes. Whether one target comparison makes the report 'progress measured against targets' (V5 decision c) is a judgment call; the lighter reading is slightly better.

MSA has three categories (note ****), but the only reported rurality result is non-MSA vs MSA principal city, a single pair (groupwise rule 1); the supplementary tables are not in the packet. Race/ethnicity is ranked across 3+ groups (highest Asian, lowest Black) and insurance has 4 levels vs Ref, so those entries stand.

brief_issues: evaluation or monitoring: the brief does not say how much target comparison makes a routine coverage report 'monitoring against targets' (one target sentence here).
